findings.mechanism: Each parsed Tree is a reference cycle (Node.parent/children, Node.tree, Tree.root/by_path), so it is freed only by the cyclic GC. tuning.install() raises the gen0 threshold from 700 to 40000, so garbage trees pile up until a collection and the memory graph climbs, then drops.
findings.cause: gc.set_threshold(40_000, 20, 20) delays cyclic collection; the cyclic structures in outlines/models.py:7-14 and :35 are normal garbage, not retained by any global.
findings.evidence: Ran 40000 conversions with OutlineService and sampled len(gc.get_objects()): it sawtooths (31k, 50k, 27k, 44k, 22k, 40k, 17k, 37k) instead of rising monotonically. RSS stayed at about 22 MB throughout. After a manual gc.collect() the count fell to 11272, the same value as after 6000 conversions. Nothing global or per-service accumulates: OutlineService holds only a counter and max_depth.
findings.discriminator: A forced gc.collect() returns the object count to the same constant baseline (11272) at both 6k and 40k iterations, and the live count drops periodically on its own. The growth is bounded, delayed garbage with no unbounded retention. Fix: lower the threshold, or break the cycles (weakref for parent/tree).
